title: Wudu in detail
hookLine: the required parts: face, arms to elbows, wiping the head, feet, and the sunnah additions

lines: A VESSEL OF WATER, SOMEONE WATCHING.
HANDS, MOUTH, NOSE, FACE, ARMS, HEAD, FEET.
I SAW HIM DO IT LIKE THIS.
cards: Uthman ibn Affan, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, asks for a vessel of water. Humran, who reports the scene, is watching. Uthman doesn't explain.
He shows. He pours water over his hands, three times. He dips his right hand in and rinses his mouth and his nose.
He washes his face, three times. His arms up to the elbows. He passes his wet hands over his head.
He washes his feet up to the ankles. Then he says: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ make wudu just like this. Sahih al-Bukhari keeps the scene, at number 159.

teach.h: THE VERSE: FACE, ARMS, HEAD, FEET.
teach.b: Year two read the wudu verse; today, the washing itself. Uthman's demonstration holds two layers, and the fiqh books separate them.

The first is in the Qur'an, 5:6, in Pickthall's translation: "O ye who believe! When ye rise up for prayer, wash your faces, and your hands up to the elbows, and lightly rub your heads and (wash) your feet up to the ankles."
Face, arms, head, feet: the required parts, without which the wudu isn't done.

teach.h: THE SUNNAH: HANDS, MOUTH, NOSE, EARS.
teach.b: The second layer is everything else Uthman showed: washing the hands first, rinsing the mouth and nose, starting on the right, doing the washings three times. Other reports add wiping the ears.
These are the sunnah additions, what the Prophet ﷺ did, and Muslims follow them as part of doing it well.

teach.h: THE SCHOOLS READ SOME WORDS DIFFERENTLY.
teach.b: Inside the verse, the schools read some words differently, and they say so openly. How much of the head must be wiped? The schools give different answers.

And the feet: Sunni schools read the verse as washing them; Shia jurists read it as wiping them. Each reads the same Arabic carefully and arrives at its own practice. Notice the verse doesn't say be pure in general.
It names a face, two arms, a head, two feet.

teach.h: LIMB BY LIMB, THEN A FOCUSED PRAYER.
teach.b: Purity, here, goes limb by limb.

teach.h: WASH YOUR FACES, AND YOUR HANDS UP TO THE ELBOWS.
teach.b: And Uthman closed by reporting that whoever makes wudu like this and then prays two units without letting the mind wander has past sins forgiven. The outer water and the inner focus, one movement.

how: Muslims make wudu before prayer by washing the face, the arms to the elbows, wiping the head, and washing or wiping the feet as their school teaches, usually adding the sunnah steps: hands, mouth, nose and ears, right before left.

o: a quick rinse of the hands only, before eating a meal
a full bath of the whole body, needed before every prayer
washing face, arms, head and feet, with the sunnah around it

games.q: wudu in detail — tap the pairs.
p: showed wudu with a vessel of water

s: the verse of wudu names each part to wash
5:6 names the face, the arms to the elbows, the head and the feet.
rinsing the mouth is one of the parts named in the verse
it's a sunnah addition, from what the Prophet did, as Uthman showed.
every school reads the verse's words the same way
they differ, for example on how much of the head, and on washing or wiping the feet.

games.q: Uthman ibn Affan wants to pass on how the Prophet made wudu. what does he do?
o: recite the verse and explain it.
call for water and show them.
leave it for others to describe.
games.why: he calls for a vessel of water and does it in front of them, then says he saw the Prophet do it like this (Bukhari 159).

practice: If you make wudu and water is near, make it now and name each limb under your breath as you wash it: hands, mouth, nose, face, arms, head, ears, feet.
If you don't, follow it where you sit, resting your attention on your hands, then your face, your forearms, the top of your head, your feet. One part at a time, each finished before the next.
